description: Federal wage-subsidy program under the Youth Employment and Skills Strategy. It funds employers to create paid summer jobs for youth; funded jobs are posted on Job Bank. Owen does not apply to the program directly — employers apply for funding, then hire youth into the funded jobs.
eligibility: Youth participants: aged 15 to 30 at the start of the job; legally entitled to work in Canada; Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected person (international students are not eligible). Jobs: 30-40 hours/week, 6-16 consecutive weeks. Employers: not-for-profits, public-sector employers, and private-sector employers with 50 or fewer full-time employees; NEW for 2027, employers must have been in operation at least 2 years by Dec 31, 2026 (exemptions exist).

key_dates.funding_decisions: Starting April 2027, all organizations notified by end of June 2027

name: Canada Summer Jobs (CSJ) 2027
notes: Most relevant to Owen as a SUMMER option, not after-school/weekend work: funded jobs are full-time (30-40 hrs/week). Owen should watch Job Bank for CSJ-funded jobs in Bowmanville/Durham in spring 2027. Subsidy: up to 100% of provincial minimum wage for not-for-profits, up to 50% for public/private employers.
status: open — employer applications open now, closing 2026-12-03

description: The federal umbrella strategy that funds organizations across Canada to deliver employability-skills sessions, employment services, and paid work experience for youth. Canada Summer Jobs is a program under YESS. Youth do not apply to YESS centrally; they join a project run by a funded local service provider.
eligibility: Aged 15 to 30 at the start of the intervention; legally entitled to work in Canada; Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person with refugee/protected-person status. Indigenous youth, racialized youth, youth living with disabilities, youth from Official Language Minority Communities, and youth from rural/remote areas may be prioritized. Individual local projects often add their own suitability rules (e.g. out of school, unemployed, facing barriers) — check the local provider.

key_dates.application_deadline: None published centrally — intake is by local funded provider, rolling or cohort-based

name: Youth Employment and Skills Strategy (YESS)
notes: Limited direct value for Owen right now: most YESS projects target youth who are out of school and/or unemployed and facing barriers, and require full-time availability. Owen is in school. No Durham Region YESS delivery provider was confirmed in this research — that is a gap to check with Employment Ontario (1-800-387-5656). Do not present any specific local YESS project as available.
status: active — ongoing federal strategy; no central application window

description: Ontario (Employment Ontario) year-round program giving youth facing multiple and/or complex barriers to employment intensive supports: paid pre-employment training, job matching, paid job placements up to 6 months, mentorship and job coaching.
eligibility: Aged 15 to 29; Ontario resident; eligible to work in Canada; unemployed; NOT attending school full time; experiencing multiple and/or complex barriers to employment. (15- to 18-year-olds must be legally excused from attending high school via a Supervised Alternative Learning agreement, per the program training guide.)

key_dates.application_deadline: None published — continuous intake reported by third-party listings; not confirmed on an ontario.ca public page

name: Ontario Youth Job Connection (YJC) — year-round
notes: LIKELY NOT ELIGIBLE FOR OWEN: the year-round stream requires the youth to be out of school and unemployed. Owen is in high school. Included so the site does not confuse it with the Summer stream. Access is through a local Employment Ontario service provider, not a direct online application.
status: active — continuous intake reported (not confirmed on ontario.ca public page)

description: The summer component of Youth Job Connection. It gives high-school students facing challenging life circumstances paid pre-employment training, help finding a summer, part-time or after-school job, a paid placement, and support transitioning back to school.
eligibility: Aged 15 to 18; Ontario resident; eligible to work in Canada; currently in high school and planning to return to school in the fall (or move on to post-secondary); facing challenging life circumstances / multiple or complex barriers to employment.

key_dates.application_deadline: None published — intake through local Employment Ontario service providers; timing not confirmed
key_dates.program_details: 20 hours of paid pre-employment training; summer job placement up to 8 weeks; up to 10 hours/week (evenings/weekends) during the school year for up to 6 months, per provider descriptions

name: Youth Job Connection Summer (YJC Summer)
notes: The most directly relevant Ontario program for Owen IF he meets the 'challenging life circumstances / barriers' suitability test — that test is assessed by the local provider, and no Durham/Bowmanville provider or intake date was confirmed in this research. The after-school hours (up to 10 hrs/week evenings/weekends) fit Owen's availability. Do not list a local contact until one is confirmed with Employment Ontario.
status: active — no published deadline; intake via local Employment Ontario provider

description: Full-time temporary summer jobs with the Ontario Public Service across ministries, agencies and partner organizations (administration, parks, environment, IT, trades support, etc.), 7-18 weeks between May and Labour Day.
eligibility: Must be a student or recent graduate: enrolled in secondary or post-secondary school (currently or for the fall semester), or graduated within 6 months of the start of the placement. Must be at least 15 years old by the first day of employment. Ontario residency and eligibility to work in Canada required.

key_dates.2026_campaign: Closed — all 2026 student summer job ads have now closed
key_dates.2027_campaign: New opportunities for summer 2027 will be posted in the fall/winter (no exact date published); check GOjobs regularly

name: Ontario Summer Employment Opportunities (SEO) — Ontario Public Service student jobs
notes: Summer-only and full-time, so not an after-school option, but a strong summer-2027 target for Owen (he meets the age and student-status tests). 2026 postings listed pay around $17.60-$18.45/hr; 2027 pay not published yet — do not quote a 2027 rate. Apply via GOjobs (gojobs.gov.on.ca), Job Category 'Student Summer Employment Opportunities'.

description: Ontario entrepreneurship program for students: start and run a small summer business with training, mentorship and a grant of up to $3,000 ($1,500 to start, up to $1,500 more on successful completion).
eligibility: Aged 15-29; Ontario student returning to high school, college or university in the fall; Ontario resident; Canadian citizen or permanent resident; not already running a business; not working at another job or in school more than 12 hours/week during the program; must not have received a Summer Company grant before. Under 18s need a parent/guardian to sign the agreement. Minimum 280 hours for high-school students over the summer.

key_dates.2027_applications: 2027-01-25 to 2027-05-21 (reported by City of Toronto and other local delivery centres; NOT yet confirmed on an ontario.ca page — verify on ontario.ca/summercompany before publishing the dates)

name: Summer Company (Ontario)

description: Paid 8-week summer jobs for youth working outdoors on natural-resources projects in their own community (e.g. creating wildlife habitat, studying species at risk), with training such as First Aid. Participants may earn two high-school co-op credits.
eligibility: Aged 16 or 17 at time of hire, and not turning 18 before December 31 of the program year. (Other eligibility details are on the Ontario.ca careers postings.)

key_dates.postings: Positions posted on Ontario.ca/careers in March and April; deadlines vary
